skill.name: azure-ai-openai-dotnet
skill.description: Reference guide for using Azure.AI.OpenAI in .NET applications, covering authentication, chat, embeddings, images, audio, tools, and Azure AI Search.

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged Markdown code fences, inline code terms, placeholder URLs, and credential variable examples. Manual review found documentation-only Azure OpenAI .NET examples, not executable automation or secret exfiltration. No prompt injection or net-new semantic security issue was found.

remediation.issue: API key examples can be copied into unsafe workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Add a visible warning to store keys in a secret manager and prefer Entra ID in production.

remediation.issue: Shell commands appear in documentation examples.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands are examples for the user to run manually, not instructions for agents to execute.

content.value_statement: Teams need clear patterns for Azure OpenAI features in .NET applications. This skill provides focused C# examples for authentication, chat, embeddings, images, audio, tools, and RAG.
actual_capabilities: Shows package setup for Azure.AI.OpenAI, OpenAI, Azure.Identity, and Azure.Search.Documents.
Demonstrates API key and Microsoft Entra ID authentication patterns.
Provides chat completion examples for basic, async, streaming, multi-turn, and option-based requests.
Covers structured outputs, reasoning model settings, and function calling with tool definitions.
Includes examples for embeddings, image generation, audio transcription, text to speech, and Azure AI Search RAG.
limitations: It is a reference guide, not a complete production application.
Examples require existing Azure resources, deployments, permissions, and package compatibility.
It does not provision Azure infrastructure or manage secrets.
SDK versions and model names should be checked against official Microsoft documentation.

use_cases.title: Start a .NET Chat Integration
use_cases.description: Build a first Azure OpenAI chat client with authentication and basic request patterns.

use_cases.title: Standardize Production Authentication
use_cases.description: Compare API key and Microsoft Entra ID patterns before setting team guidance.

use_cases.title: Add RAG and Multimodal Features
use_cases.description: Extend an application with embeddings, Azure AI Search, image generation, or audio features.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Chat Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show the simplest Azure OpenAI chat setup for a .NET console app using Microsoft Entra ID.

prompt_templates.title: Add Streaming Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to adapt my existing chat completion flow to stream responses and handle long answers.

prompt_templates.title: Design a RAG Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a .NET Azure AI Search RAG flow with authentication, citations, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Tools and Structured Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a .NET flow that validates tool call arguments and returns structured output for a business task.

output_examples.input: Create a basic Azure OpenAI chat setup for .NET.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan covering required packages, Entra ID authentication, ChatClient creation, and a simple prompt-response flow.

output_examples.input: Add RAG to an existing chat endpoint.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step outline for configuring Azure AI Search data sources, passing citations, and handling missing context.

output_examples.input: Compare API key and Entra ID authentication.
output_examples.output: A short recommendation that favors Entra ID for production and reserves API keys for controlled local testing or demos.

best_practices: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities for production authentication.
Validate tool call arguments before executing any application function.
Track token usage, rate limits, retries, and timeouts in production services.
anti_patterns: Do not commit API keys or endpoint secrets to source control.
Do not copy examples without matching them to your deployed model names.
Do not execute model tool calls without schema validation and authorization checks.

faq.question: Does this skill write Azure infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It explains .NET SDK usage and assumes resources already exist.

faq.question: Can it help with non-Azure OpenAI clients?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Azure-compatible use of the OpenAI .NET SDK.

faq.question: Does it require API keys?
faq.answer: No. It recommends Microsoft Entra ID for production and also shows API key examples.

faq.question: Does it include RAG guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows Azure AI Search integration concepts and citation handling.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should I verify package versions?
faq.answer: Yes. Check Microsoft documentation and NuGet before production use.
